author: HSinghHira
tagline: Self-hosted file management and cloud storage
description:
Cloudreve is an open-source, self-hosted file management and sharing platform — think a private Dropbox or Google Drive that you fully control, with support for ten different storage backends.
**Features**
- Drag-and-drop uploads, in-browser previews, and shareable public
  links with optional passwords and expiration.

- Native WebDAV support for mounting Cloudreve as a network drive on
  Windows, macOS, or Linux.

- Ten storage backends supported — Local, S3-compatible (MinIO,
  Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, AWS S3), OneDrive, Aliyun OSS, Tencent
  COS, and more — assignable per user group.

- Optional Aria2/qBittorrent integration for remote downloads
  straight to your storage.

- PostgreSQL for application data and Redis for caching, both
  bundled and pre-wired.

- Persistent storage under /DATA/AppData/$AppID for app data,
  Postgres, and Redis.

**How to use?**
1. Open Cloudreve from the ZimaAppStore dashboard.
2. Register an account — the first account created becomes the
   administrator.

3. Start uploading files and creating folders under the default
   Local storage policy.

4. Optional: connect an S3-compatible bucket or other remote backend
   from the admin panel so uploads survive beyond this host.

5. Optional: enable WebDAV in your user settings to mount Cloudreve
   as a network drive, or enable Aria2 remote downloads in the admin
   panel (uses the published 8410 port).

6. Further server settings — storage policies, user groups, sharing
   rules — are all configured later through the in-app Admin Panel,
   no compose file edits needed.

tips.before_install:
1. Open the app configuration before starting the installation.
2. Find the CHANGEME_DB_PASSWORD placeholder in both the
   cloudreve service (CR_CONF_Database.Password) and the postgres
   service (POSTGRES_PASSWORD).

3. Replace both CHANGEME_DB_PASSWORD values with the same strong
   password — they must match exactly.

4. Confirm both values match before starting the install; a
   mismatch surfaces as a database connection failure, not a clear
   error message.

5. Start the Cloudreve installation.
6. Wait for the postgres and redis containers to report healthy
   (service_healthy) before opening Cloudreve — this is handled
   automatically via depends_on, no action needed.

7. Open Cloudreve from the ZimaAppStore dashboard.
8. Register an account — the first account you create automatically
   becomes the administrator, so register your own account first
   before sharing access with anyone else.

9. All further configuration (storage backends, user groups,
   sharing policies, WebDAV, remote downloads) lives in the in-app
   Admin Panel — no need to touch this file again.

10. Important: POSTGRES_PASSWORD and CR_CONF_Database.Password
    only take effect the way you'd expect at first run — changing
    either later without updating the other, or without also
    updating the already-initialized Postgres user's password,
    will lock Cloudreve out of the database until you manually
    reset it (or start from a fresh volume).
